ROUND 1 performance verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES.
Subject: pr:330
Head: 1c998e75d005eaa70266314da25a533204ab7f70
Answers: 01a1ff60-5b69-7623-959e-b1ba867b05a6

The healthy shutdown path reduces two write launches per owned pane to one batched write launch, and keeping the control client until detach finishes removes the previous release/read race. The source and real-tmux CI witness support this launch reduction. No new steady-state per-pane launch/tick is introduced. No demonstrated new normal-use resource-cost breach blocks this head; actual fleet shutdown improvement remains owed after deployment.

Verified cost:
- Normal nonempty detach with a healthy control client: ONE run("pipe-pane detach taps") and TWO scoped list-panes tap-state reads, initial and verify. run records tmux.pipe-pane detach taps before executing through the existing resolved-program launch path. The real-tmux32-pane witness warms the client, asserts exactly one process launch and successful cleanup, and leaves its unowned foreign tap intact.
- Empty/no-listed-owned work can need zero writes. With B batch rounds, there are B write-site attempts and normally1+B tap-state reads. A control read returning Fork launches through the existing counted run path; startup/replacement/fallback can add launches. One batch write is not an unconditional one-process ceiling for a degraded stop, nor a whole-daemon-stop launch count.
- The before model is two write launches per extant owned pane (pipe-pane, clear owner), plus possible forked list/display reads after the racing control release. About145 panes therefore implies about290 writes before read fallbacks, not an independently measured290-launch counter delta. The new release sequence waits for observer shutdown/detach before releasing the client, independently of the HTTP-drain join.
- "Nothing per pane" is true only of the normal write-launch COUNT. Command clauses/argv, ownership checks, result bookkeeping, local map removals and one sink unlink per successfully released pane remain O(P) work. Each tap snapshot parses every pane in adapter scope N into a map, not just requested P. There is no new repeated ledger rewrite in release_tap.
- The convergence loop retries every25ms while a listed pending pane remains piped OR has any marker. This includes command failures/non-convergence, not only a pane closed mid-list. Each retry can add another batch launch and full scoped verify read. The2s grace starts after the initial snapshot/ownership work and is checked AFTER run and verify. run uses synchronous Command::output without a child timeout:2s is not a hard detach/phase wall-time ceiling. No demonstrated new hang is asserted; the blocking launcher is inherited.
- Single-pane retirement still calls detach_pane_tap, but that provided method now delegates to the batch path. Its healthy case therefore has one combined write rather than the previous two writes, and two scoped tap snapshots rather than the old per-pane display verification. The caller remains one call per retired pane; adapter cost is not literally unchanged. No regular living-pane loop gains a launch.
- Phase topology stays constant-sized. HTTP drain is started earlier, so its phase line measures its own operation. Observer completion/error is awaited before the blocking control release is started; an inner observer panic becomes a result and still reaches release. AbortOnDrop cancels owned phase tasks at async cancellation points, not synchronous tmux calls or already-started spawn_blocking work. It is not a hard kill/time bound on every child.
- #325 cost notes are correctly folded into the source/docs: window-plus-new-retirement traversal, all-window/live-roster/role work and per-daemon wall-clock cooldown. Rendering is only on the alarm path (at most20 displayed IDs), not each sweep. No new alarm cadence or launcher flag behavior is introduced.

Nonblocking notes owed:
1. Correct the cost row to "no per-pane launches", not no per-pane work; name scoped snapshot, argv/command and sink-unlink scaling. Single-pane retirement's call site is unchanged, but its adapter work changed.
2. Keep the1-launch statement scoped to the healthy converged batch. Count retries/read fallbacks separately; the retry condition is broader than pane disappearance, and2s is convergence grace, not a child/stop deadline. These details were sent to the independent correctness reviewer.
3. AFTER, explicitly owed: the next authorized bounce's pane-observer phase duration against4731ms at approximately145 panes, with actual tracked/owned-pane counts, deployed head/process and control-release ordering. Keep retry/fallback launch evidence if available. Do not subtract spawn counters across old/new daemon PIDs; the passive BEFORE below is not detach proof.

BEFORE receipt and provenance:
- Independently read the requested4731ms line in the existing daemon log: observer started2026-11-21T16:53:38.298986Z, ended16:53:43.030672Z. Control release ended16:53:38.305906Z (6ms), before observer detach finished. This is November22 at02:53 local(+10), not the currently live83182's stop.
- The source lines do not stamp a PID or pane count. Approximately145 panes is the PM/coder's cohort statement, not measured by these four lines. The active daemon83182 started later, at03:14:36 local; its PID cannot be assigned to the older stop. The log also has a later4666ms observer stop at17:14:36.430171Z UTC. Neither line is AFTER for this PR. Targeted receipt preserved in files/pr330-stop-before.json; no credential file or unrelated log content was copied.

All daemon spawn counters flat(delta0); CPU3:23.98->3:24.60(+0.62s, about3.1% of one core), RSS91856->91808KiB. No stop, tap mutation or alarm induced. This cannot measure the new batch site before deployment.

Nine focused cases passed: real-tmux single-launch/foreign-tap test, cancelled-stop phase test, safe alarm rendering test and all six spawn-site guards.
- The32-pane test removes the gone pane BEFORE the initial detach snapshot. It proves the ordinary one-launch path, not an independently induced mid-list-close race. Its scaled5s assertion is fixture proof, not a fleet wall-time ceiling. Producer D1-D3 results and the zero-tap real-stop excerpt were inspected, not independently rerun or claimed as fleet AFTER.
- harness boot ready=false(missing vitest); harness checks --quick --json exit1, eight dependency/ambient-tool failures; pij-skill/native/SDK pass, heavy Rust/route/smoke skipped. Local gate is not green; C25 exact-head CI is separate proof. No dependency links/install, local Rust build or private tmux test run.
- No product edits, bounce, live detach, working-seat mutation or production DB access. Only the owned CI download is temporary; source/measurement receipts persist in session files. Independent correctness/security verdicts remain separate. Hold performance/330 until merge; AFTER obligation survives the merge.

Policy/brakes: process-local/expected-marker ownership decides which taps may be detached: the existing POLICY. Verification/grace can retain a sink/marker and report failure, never authorize a different tap: BRAKES. The known pre-existing late-cat empty-sink race(D-F267-4) remains stated, not fixed by this launch reduction.

Harness lesson / magicWand: emit detach rounds, initial/pending pane counts and the final old-daemon batch/fallback launch counters with the shutdown phase line, so the next AFTER proves both reduced launches and latency without guessing across a PID reset.
